description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of two multilingual BERT models — mBERT and XLM-R — across various language families in terms of task count, categorized by whether one model performed better, worse, or the same as the other. The horizontal axis lists nine language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “task count,” ranges from 0 to 40 in increments of 10, indicating the number of probing tasks where a model outperformed or matched the other. Each language family has three grouped bars: light gray for “mBERT better,” dark gray for “XLM-R better,” and olive green for “same.” For example, in IE-Slavic, XLM-R significantly outperforms mBERT with nearly 40 tasks where it is better, while mBERT is better in about 12 tasks and they are equal in about 28. In contrast, for IE-Indic, both models perform similarly, with only a few tasks favoring either model. The chart visually emphasizes that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT across most language families, particularly in IE-Slavic and Uralic, while mBERT shows a slight edge only in IE-Germanic and IE-Romance. The legend in the top-right corner clarifies the color coding for “better” outcomes and “same” performance.
